observed_evidence: Transactions per store in S03, S04 and S05 fell 27.8% against 1.1% in the matched control stores (S07, S09, S12, S16, S18); a single step change on 15 Jul 2025 (S03 16 Jul, S04 9 Jul, S05 21 Jul). Their transactions were still 28% below the control-store path in retail week 52, the last week of the data.
financial_relevance: High. Estimated excess decline -€397,778 (54% of the change), range -€435,210 to -€377,245 across control groups and windows. ESTIMATE of an observed change, measured against the control stores; not a measured loss and not a cause.
what_we_know: The loss is in the number of receipts, across all categories, weekdays and hours. Basket value (€45.06 vs €45.51 in the controls), prices, promotion share, availability and return rate moved like the control stores. No internal lever in the data explains it. Caveats carried from Phase 6: no matched control store is in Dublin (the cluster's region), and the three stores were picked in Phase 5 because they fell most, so the placebo test overstates significance; using the two other Dublin stores as controls gives a similar size (-€404,846).
what_we_do_not_know: Why customers made fewer purchases: fewer visitors, lower conversion, a change in the stores (hours, closures, works, staffing) that is not recorded in the model, or something outside the stores. Whether it has recovered since the end of the data.
business_risk: The largest single component of the decline and it had not recovered by the end of the data. Acting on a guessed cause (price cuts, local marketing) could spend money without effect, while the real cause continues.
immediate_safe_action: Confirm the receipt counts are complete for the three stores; collect the operational and local data listed; run structured area-manager visits; track the gap to the control stores weekly. No price, promotion or marketing response aimed at these stores until a cause is identified.
investigation_required: A staged investigation (see the investigation sequence): data completeness first, then store operations, footfall and conversion, then the local environment, then customer behaviour.
additional_data_required: DR01 POS transaction completeness check; DR02 Store operating logs; DR03 Staffing coverage; DR04 Footfall; DR05 Conversion rate; DR06 Queue and waiting-time indicators; DR07 Competitor activity; DR08 Local environment; DR09 Customer feedback; DR10 Loyalty and customer frequency; DR11 Online and channel data
supporting_teams: Commercial (PROPOSED); Store managers S03 to S05 (PROPOSED); Data/BI (PROPOSED); Finance (PROPOSED)
kpi_to_monitor: Transactions per store YoY, cluster vs matched controls (weekly gap); footfall and conversion once available
trigger_escalation: Escalate to the Head of Retail if the weekly gap to the control stores widens further, or if another store shows a step change of the same kind (early-warning signal EW01).
review_frequency: Weekly during the investigation; monthly after a decision
decision_after_investigation: If a store-side cause is found (hours, closure, works, staffing): fix it and track the gap back toward the controls. If a temporary external cause (road works, local disruption): monitor to its end date. If a lasting external cause (for example a new competitor): decide a commercial response and test it against control stores before rolling it out. If nothing is found: keep it reported as UNRESOLVED and keep monitoring; do not assign a cause.

observed_evidence: Electronics & Tech availability fell from 95.4% to 89.3%; full-week stock-outs (store-SKU-weeks with no stock all week) rose from 0 to 786, of which 674 on Voltix Distribution Ltd SKUs (prior year 0). Zero units were sold in every full-week stock-out.
financial_relevance: Medium. Estimated lost sales €37,235 gross (5% of the change); €23,963 net of the demand that came back after restock (€13,272); sensitivity range €23,963 to €44,460. ESTIMATE. 61% of the lost sales sits in the top 10% of SKUs by prior-year sales (the Phase 6 definition); the three largest SKUs (P00149, P00150, P00151) hold 50%.
cause_note: D03: Established only for lost sales during full-week stock-outs; why stock ran out: not established (I3)
what_we_know: The mechanism is visible: no stock, no sales. It is concentrated in a small number of high-selling SKUs. Some demand returned after restock, so part of the gross loss was deferred rather than lost.
what_we_do_not_know: Why stock ran out (see I3). How much was lost in partial-week stock-outs (only weekly snapshots are available). How much demand moved to other SKUs.
business_risk: Small in the decline, but it is the one mechanism the evidence establishes, and it affects the highest-selling SKUs, which customers notice.
immediate_safe_action: A weekly zero-stock exception list for the fastest-selling Electronics SKUs on current sales (including new launches), starting with the three SKUs with the largest lost-sales estimates (P00149, P00150, P00151), routed to replenishment; a review of reorder points and safety stock for the most affected SKUs against current sales rates. These are internal replenishment controls and do not assume the supplier is at fault.
investigation_required: Request daily stock positions so partial-week stock-outs can be measured; the cause of the stock shortfall is investigated under I3.
additional_data_required: DR12 Daily stock positions; DR13 DC availability; DR14 Store replenishment and allocation rules
supporting_teams: Store Operations (PROPOSED); Electronics & Tech buying (PROPOSED); Data/BI (PROPOSED)
kpi_to_monitor: Electronics & Tech availability; full-week stock-outs; zero-stock weeks on the top-selling SKUs
trigger_escalation: Escalate if a top-selling SKU has a full-week stock-out in two consecutive weeks, or if category availability stays below its prior-year level for four weeks (early-warning signals EW03 and EW04).
decision_after_investigation: Keep the exception list if availability on the listed SKUs improves; keep, reverse or make permanent the temporary parameter changes only after I3 shows whether ordering or supply limited stock.

issue: Voltix Distribution Ltd stock-out concentration (supply vs ordering)
observed_evidence: Voltix stock-out episodes rose from 609 to 1,181 and their mean length from 1.1 to 2.1 weeks. The SKU stock-out rate rose 6.8 pp more than for other suppliers' SKUs. Opening stock of its SKUs fell while weekly receipts per SKU did not.
financial_relevance: Low. €30,996 (83%) of the €37,235 lost-sales estimate sits on Voltix SKUs. Part of I2: not an additional amount.
what_we_know: The concentration is statistically robust (it survives leaving out any single SKU).
what_we_do_not_know: Whether Voltix delivered less or later than ordered, or Brightwater ordered or replenished less. The data has receipts, not orders.
business_risk: Blaming or re-sourcing a supplier without order and delivery evidence could damage a relationship and would not fix an internal ordering problem.
immediate_safe_action: Collect purchase orders, confirmations, ASNs and receipts for Voltix SKUs; share the stock pattern with Voltix as joint fact-finding, not as a performance claim. No penalty, delisting or re-sourcing decision until the order and delivery data are reviewed.
investigation_required: Compare what was ordered, confirmed, shipped and received, and when, for H2 2024 and H2 2025; compare order quantities with Brightwater's own ordering parameters and forecasts; check DC availability and store allocation rules for these SKUs.
additional_data_required: DR15 Purchase orders; DR16 Supplier confirmations and ASNs; DR17 Supplier fill rate and OTIF; DR18 Lead times and late deliveries; DR19 Ordering parameters; DR20 Demand forecasts and forecast accuracy; DR21 Supplier service levels
supporting_teams: Electronics & Tech buying (supplier relationship) (PROPOSED); Commercial (supplier sanction decisions) (PROPOSED); Finance (PROPOSED); Voltix account manager (PROPOSED)
kpi_to_monitor: Supplier fill rate and OTIF (not available yet); Voltix SKU availability
trigger_escalation: Escalate to the Commercial Director if order data shows short or late supply; to the Supply Chain Manager if it shows Brightwater under-ordered.
review_frequency: Fortnightly until the order data is reviewed
decision_after_investigation: Supplier-side cause: raise it through the supplier review with the evidence (fill rate, OTIF, lead time). Ordering-side cause: correct parameters or forecasts. Both or neither: document it and keep monitoring.

observed_evidence: Refunds recorded with the reason 'Faulty' rose by €31,589 (+90%). The top five stores (S13, S14, S07, S15, S16) hold 89% of the gross increase; the rise starts mainly with items sold from September 2025 (2.7 'Faulty' returns per 100 units sold for September 2025 sales against 1.0 a year earlier). Other return reasons did not rise materially (the largest change, 'Damaged', was +€484).
financial_relevance: Low. -€31,589 (4% of the change): a FACT (recorded refunds), range -€31,589 to -€26,226 depending on the rate basis. The share is small; the question is quality and process, not size.
what_we_know: The increase is in the recorded till reason, concentrated in five stores and in recent sale months, and spread across products (the top five products hold only 53%) and across all four suppliers.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether the products are defective. A till reason is not an inspection result. The pattern fits a batch problem, a supplier problem, a change in how those stores record returns, a store process, customer behaviour or another cause; the data cannot choose between them.
business_risk: If products are defective, faulty stock may still be on sale and customers affected; supplier claim windows may apply (check the contracts). If it is a recording practice, the returns data is misleading for every later analysis.
immediate_safe_action: Keep 'Faulty' Electronics returns in the five stores, and a comparison sample from three other stores, for inspection instead of disposing of or returning them unexamined, and record batch, lot or serial numbers; audit how the five stores apply the 'Faulty' reason; request supplier RMA and warranty data.
investigation_required: QA inspection of returned units; batch and serial analysis; supplier RMA and warranty comparison; a returns-handling audit against comparison stores; see the classification framework.
additional_data_required: DR22 QA inspection results; DR23 Batch, lot and serial numbers; DR24 Supplier RMA and defect reports; DR25 Warranty claims and repair outcomes; DR26 Returns-handling audit; DR27 Customer complaints about product faults; DR28 Delivery route serving the five stores
supporting_teams: Store Operations (returns process) (PROPOSED); Customer Service (PROPOSED); Supplier quality contacts (PROPOSED); Data/BI (PROPOSED)
kpi_to_monitor: 'Faulty' returned units per 100 sold, by store and by sale month; QA confirmed-defect rate (not available yet)
trigger_escalation: Escalate to the Quality lead at once if inspection confirms a defect in a batch still on sale; escalate if the 'Faulty' rate rises in stores outside the five (early-warning signal EW05).
review_frequency: Fortnightly until inspection results are in; monthly after
decision_after_investigation: Confirmed defect in a batch or supplier: a quality decision (withdraw the batch, supplier claim) owned by Quality. Recording practice: clarify the reason codes and retrain, and restate the KPI. Neither: keep monitoring and report the cause as unresolved.

observed_evidence: The Home & Kitchen discount rate rose from 2.4% to 11.9% of gross sales and promotion events from 2,427 to 8,848; promotion share of sales from 12.7% to 27.6%. Category net revenue fell €239,994, units 2.8%, and average selling price from €29.78 to €27.79.
financial_relevance: High. Attribution uses M1: -€186,146 (25% of the change). The four Phase 6 methods disagree: M1 -€186,146, M4 -€265,003, M2 +€97,505, M3 +€79,059. They are shown separately and never added. Point estimates run from -€265,003 (M4) to +€97,505 (M2), and -€380,272 to +€161,234 including their intervals: even the sign is uncertain.
what_we_know: Promotions became deeper and more frequent while the category fell against other categories in the same stores and weeks, mostly through price rather than volume.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether the promotions caused the decline or added revenue: incrementality, pull-forward, cannibalisation and the right baseline are all unresolved, because back-to-back promotions (64% of current-year events) contaminate the baselines.
business_risk: Cutting promotions on the strength of M1 or M4 could remove revenue if M2 and M3 are right; continuing unchanged could keep eroding margin if M1 and M4 are right.
immediate_safe_action: Every new Home & Kitchen promotion deeper than the prior-year depth needs a written objective and a planned post-event review on margin as well as sales; no blanket cut and no blanket increase.
investigation_required: A promotion review of the H2 2025 calendar (objectives, planned vs actual depth, funding), then a controlled test of promotion depth; see the test design.
additional_data_required: DR29 Promotion calendar with objectives; DR30 Planned vs actual discount depth; DR31 Supplier promotional funding; DR32 Controlled test results; DR33 SKU-level price elasticities and customer segments
kpi_to_monitor: Home & Kitchen discount rate, promotion share, gross margin %; promotion incrementality once a test exists
trigger_escalation: Escalate if the discount rate or promotion share rises above the approved plan, or if category gross margin % falls a further step (early-warning signal EW07).
review_frequency: Monthly; weekly while a test runs
decision_after_investigation: At the post-test gate (after the test and its post-period, planned around day 150 to 180): keep the depth the test shows adds net margin; move towards the prior-year depth only where the test shows it loses margin. An inconclusive test is not a reason to cut: keep the current depth under the governance control and extend or repeat the test. Until then, do not claim an effect either way.

issue: Electronics & Tech range and continuing-SKU sales
observed_evidence: Outside the cluster, new Electronics SKUs added €265,233, delisted SKUs lost €95,472 and continuing SKUs sold €294,304 less, mostly through lower sales per ranged week.
financial_relevance: Not quantified. A partition of the category change (FACT), not an estimate of a cause; not added to the attribution. Most of the unattributed residual sits here (see I7).
what_we_know: The range change itself added revenue; the decline sits in continuing SKUs.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether shoppers switched to the new models, partial-week stock-outs cut sales, or substitution during stock-outs explains it.
business_risk: Low on its own; misreading it could lead to delisting SKUs whose sales simply moved to newer models.
immediate_safe_action: None beyond monitoring continuing, new and delisted SKU sales monthly.
investigation_required: Link range plan and delisting dates to SKU sales; use customer purchase history (if loyalty data exists) to see switching between models.
additional_data_required: DR12 Daily stock positions; DR34 Range plan and delisting dates; DR35 Customer-level purchase history
kpi_to_monitor: Continuing-SKU sales per ranged store-week; new and delisted SKU sales
trigger_escalation: Review if continuing-SKU sales per ranged week fall further while new-SKU sales do not rise.
decision_after_investigation: If switching explains it: no action (a normal range cycle). If partial-week stock-outs explain it: fold into I2. If neither: keep in the residual investigation.

observed_evidence: -€78,522 (11% of the change) is not attributed to any driver. By where it sits: other stores' Electronics change not explained by stock-outs or 'Faulty' returns -€88,168; other stores' Home & Kitchen change beyond M1 +€40,069; other stores' other categories +€461; the cluster's change at the control-store rate -€30,884.
financial_relevance: Medium. UNEXPLAINED / NOT ATTRIBUTED. The remainder of the attribution, so it also absorbs the uncertainty of every estimate above. Not assigned to any driver.
what_we_know: Outside the cluster, categories other than Electronics and Home & Kitchen were flat, so it is not estate-wide softness. Most of it is Electronics continuing-SKU sales outside the cluster.
what_we_do_not_know: What drives it. Forcing it into an existing explanation would overstate that explanation.
business_risk: Low on its own; the risk is analytical: hiding it would make the explanation look more complete than it is.
immediate_safe_action: No operational action. Decompose it further by store, category, product, week, price, mix, returns and availability, and check the data behind it.
additional_data_required: DR12 Daily stock positions; DR35 Customer-level purchase history; DR36 Market data for Electronics & Tech
kpi_to_monitor: Unattributed share of the change at each future period review
trigger_escalation: Re-examine if the unattributed share grows in the next period's attribution.
decision_after_investigation: Attribute a part only where a new driver meets the Phase 6 evidence standard; keep the rest labelled NOT ATTRIBUTED.
